title.rendered: The Spirit Helps Us in Our Weakness: The Gospel For Today

excerpt.rendered: You do not have to know how to pray. You only have to come. The Spirit Himself helps you in your weakness and intercedes through you with sighs too deep for words.

content.rendered:
You do not have to know how to pray. You only have to come. The Spirit Himself helps you in your weakness and intercedes through you with sighs too deep for words.

The Gospel For Today | Wednesday, June 3, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“In the same way, the Spirit helps us in our weakness. We do not know what we ought to pray for, but the Spirit himself intercedes for us through wordless groans.”
Romans 8:26 (NIV)

Today’s Message

Prayer can feel like the hardest thing in the Christian life. Not because we do not want to pray, but because, in our most honest moments, we do not know what to say. We do not know how the situation should resolve. We do not know what is the right thing to ask for. The words run out. The mind runs out. And the silence sits there like a wall.

Paul writes Romans 8:26 to people who know that silence. He does not scold them for not knowing how to pray. He brings them comfort that most Christians never quite hear properly. We do not know what we ought to pray for, he writes. The implication is breath-taking: not knowing how to pray is not a Christian failure. It is a Christian assumption. The whole posture of New Testament prayer is built around the truth that we, on our own, are not capable.

And then the gospel news: the Spirit Himself helps us. He does not wait for you to figure out the perfect prayer. He comes alongside you in the very weakness that has been silencing you. He intercedes from inside you, through wordless groans, sighs too deep for language. The longings of your heart that you cannot articulate are not lost to God. They are being carried by the Spirit, in language deeper than English or Yoruba or Spanish, straight into the throne room.

This means the prayer of a believer never fails to reach God just because the words ran out. The Spirit translates your silence. He translates your tears. He translates the groan you breathe when you put your head in your hands because you do not know what to do. None of it is wasted. All of it is heard.

So pray today. Pray with words when you have them. Pray with silence when you do not. Bring what you have. The Spirit who lives in you is praying with you, in you, and for you, with sighs too deep for words.

Prayer

Father, thank You that Your Spirit prays with me and through me when I cannot find the words. Thank You that my silences are not silent before You. Thank You that my groans are heard. Today, I trust that the Spirit who searches my heart is also lifting it to You. Pray through me. Pray for me. Pray in the gaps where my own prayers run dry. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

The Holy Spirit prays in me. I am not alone in prayer. Even when the words run out, my prayers are heard, because the Spirit Himself intercedes for me with sighs too deep for words. I come to the Father with confidence. My weakness is not a barrier to prayer. It is the doorway through which the Spirit prays.
